title: 5 ways AI is replacing SEO (and 4 things that aren’t changing)
summary: Will AI replace SEO? Yes, by expanding search and taking clicks from publishers. But 4 things stay the same.
body_markdown:
Will AI replace SEO? Many articles say no, for various reasons: Google still dominates, AI depends on web content, and SEO work still needs people.


These points have merit, but “no” is too simple an answer. AI **is** replacing parts of SEO and changing others. Publishers and businesses that rely on informational traffic are bleeding clicks, and the sooner we acknowledge AI’s impact on SEO, the faster we can adapt.


That said, a handful of tried-and-tested SEO fundamentals still hold. And they’ll continue to hold, so long as people keep searching for answers to questions. Here are five things AI is changing about SEO and four fundamentals it won’t replace.


## 5 things AI is changing about SEO


AI is changing[SEO](https://www.semrush.com/blog/what-is-seo/) by expanding search beyond Google, taking clicks from publishers, automating routine SEO tasks, adding new metrics to track, and even changing the name of the discipline.


### 1. Search continues expanding beyond Google


People are increasingly turning to AI assistants for answers, not just Google. If those assistants don’t mention or cite your brand, you’re harder to find — and you’re missing out on potential revenue.


For example,[66% of AI-using U.S. B2B professionals](https://www.semrush.com/blog/how-ai-shapes-b2b-buying/) we surveyed between March and April 2026 regularly use AI assistants to research vendors and solutions.


On the consumer side,[77.6% of U.S. consumers](https://searchengineland.com/new-data-77-use-ai-to-shop-nearly-1-in-3-wont-let-it-spend-475614) surveyed by Exploding Topics use AI assistants for shopping, and almost half said they use AI for shopping every week.


That said, searching on platforms other than Google isn’t a new phenomenon. People have already been turning to YouTube, TikTok, Reddit, and Amazon, among others, for answers. AI assistants just provide one more search surface.


#### How to adapt your visibility strategy


Adapt your visibility strategy by earning AI mentions and citations, not just search rankings. Start by checking your brand’s prominence in AI answers (we’ll share how below). Then, take steps to[optimize your site for AI search](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-search-optimization/) .


But don’t neglect Google, which is still a dominant traffic source. Even though AI traffic grew approximately 66% in 2025, it made up[only 0.14% of total web traffic](https://www.semrush.com/blog/traffic-channel-mix-study/) , compared with around 16% for organic search, according to our 2026 AI traffic mix study.


Just because people use ChatGPT doesn’t mean they’re Googling less. In fact, ChatGPT users[ran 2.1 more Google Search sessions a week](https://www.semrush.com/blog/google-usage-after-chatgpt-adoption/) after they started using ChatGPT, according to our study of Google usage after ChatGPT adoption.


As a whole, search is expanding, not disappearing. Searching is basic human behavior; people will always look for answers before they decide or buy. AI is just changing **where** they ask — not **whether** they ask.


### 2. AI is taking clicks from publishers


Publishers are losing clicks whenever AI assistants and Google’s[AI Overviews](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-overviews/) answer users’ questions, whether these are simple informational queries or multi-criteria product recommendations.


In January 2025,[91.3%](https://www.semrush.com/blog/semrush-ai-overviews-study/) of queries that triggered an AI Overview were informational, according to our 2025 AI Overviews study. This percentage fell to 57.1% in October 2025 as AI Overviews expanded into more commercial and transactional queries.


For years, publishing information online was a reliable strategy for driving traffic. That’s no longer the case now that AI systems can provide direct answers. And as a result, sites built on simple informational content have lost significant traffic and revenue.


Take education technology company Chegg: it saw global non-subscriber traffic fall[19%](https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2024-11-12-chegg-inc-stock/) year over year in Q3 2024. By January 2025, the decline reached[49%](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364954/000136495425000011/a9901-financialresultsq420.htm) , with the company blaming AI Overviews and students’ shift to generative AI tools.


#### How to adapt your business strategy


Don’t try to out-answer AI on simple questions. Instead, adapt your business strategy by competing where it can’t follow. Here’s how:


- **Assess your exposure** : Identify the queries, particularly simple informational ones, that AI can easily answer. Check how much of your traffic depends on them, so you can decide whether they’re worth defending.
- **Create non-commodity content for queries with high business value** : Non-commodity content, like research studies and first-hand reviews, provides unique insights AI can’t replicate from existing information. As a result, AI assistants are more likely to mention and cite it. We cover how to create non-commodity content below.
- **Build brand authority** : Doing this helps drive[branded searches](https://www.semrush.com/blog/branded-search/) , where users look for information specifically from your brand instead of anyone who has published an answer to their question. More on building brand authority later.
- **Offer more than information** : Develop goods, services, or experiences AI assistants can’t replicate yet. For example, instead of selling online informational courses, offer a mentorship program where students meet you one-on-one for advice tailored to their situation.


### 3. AI is automating routine SEO tasks


AI can speed up, and in some cases fully automate, routine SEO tasks like keyword clustering, metadata generation, basic technical audits, and SEO reporting. As a result, work that once took hours may now take just minutes to complete.


In our early 2026 survey of 100 marketers,[60%](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-seo/) said they use AI assistants for[keyword research](https://www.semrush.com/blog/keyword-research/) . Twenty-six percent used AI to generate page titles and meta descriptions, while 24% used it to optimize content with secondary keywords.


Only about one in five respondents drafted articles with AI.


Automation is a less controversial change to SEO in the age of AI, but we can’t automate SEO work completely. Knowing which tasks we can delegate to AI, and what a good result looks like, still involves human judgment — and that takes time to develop.


#### How to adapt your SEO workflow


Adapt your SEO workflow by handing repeatable tasks to AI. For ideas on where to start, see our guide to using[AI for SEO](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-seo/) .


Then, put the time you free up toward strategy. With AI handling repetitive execution, you can spend more time understanding your audience and deciding which content is worth creating.


Always check AI’s work before using it. Validate AI-generated keyword ideas, URLs, reports, and other output, so you don’t base your content or decisions on hallucinated, inaccurate information.


### 4. Rankings and organic traffic no longer give the full search visibility picture


Rankings and organic traffic are still important, but they can’t show how visible you are in AI search or how much AI search contributes to your business.


Ranking on page one doesn’t guarantee your content appears in AI-generated answers. In our study of 200,000 keywords, AI Overviews typically cited[fewer than three](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-overviews-study/) of the top 10 organic results. Separately, ChatGPT cites pages ranking in positions 21+ for related queries[almost 90% of the time](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-search-seo-traffic-study/) , according to our study on AI search’s impact on SEO traffic.


While branded organic traffic may reflect some of the people who visit your site after seeing your brand in an AI answer, AI traffic is still worth tracking separately. Non-Google Search visitors, like those coming from ChatGPT, are[4.4 times](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-search-seo-traffic-study/) as valuable as organic visitors based on conversion rate.


#### How to adapt the way you measure search visibility


Measure[AI visibility](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-visibility/) and traffic alongside rankings, organic traffic, and conversions to get a comprehensive view of your search visibility and how it contributes to your bottom line.


AI visibility metrics to measure include:


- **Mentions** : How often AI search platforms name your brand in their answers
- **Citations** : How often AI search platforms link to your pages as a source
- **Share of voice** : How often your brand appears in AI answers to non-branded questions compared to competitors


Our[AI Visibility Toolkit](https://www.semrush.com/ai-seo/overview/) provides a range of reports for tracking AI visibility. For example, the Visibility Overview report shows your mentions, citations, and distribution across AI search engines, while the Brand Performance report displays your share of voice.


The[Position Tracking](https://www.semrush.com/position-tracking/) tool also shows whether you appear in AI Overviews for your target keywords, alongside your rankings for them.


You can also track AI traffic in Google Analytics 4. Learn how to set it up in our[AI referral traffic](https://www.semrush.com/blog/ai-referral-traffic/) article.


As you track organic traffic, measure branded search volume separately to gauge the number of visitors who Googled your brand after learning about it from an AI answer. We share tactics for tracking branded searches in our guide to[branded search](https://www.semrush.com/blog/branded-search/) .


### 5. “SEO” is taking on new names (GEO, AEO, and more)


As AI search grows, SEOs have coined various terms for the work of optimizing for it, including[generative engine optimization](https://www.semrush.com/blog/generative-engine-optimization/) (GEO), answer engine optimization (AEO), large language model optimization (LLMO), and AI search optimization.


Here’s what each term roughly means:


- **GEO** : Shaping how your brand appears in large language models’ training data
- **AEO** : Making your content easy for AI systems to find and cite in their answers
- **LLMO** : Building your brand’s presence in large language models
- **AI search optimization** : Improving your visibility across AI search platforms


In practice, marketers often use them interchangeably to refer to the same goal of getting seen in AI answers.


#### How to adapt to the new terminology


What you call the “SEO” discipline isn’t as important as what you do to stay visible as people turn to AI for answers. Optimizing for AI mentions, citations, and share of voice builds on existing SEO work rather than replacing it.


## 4 SEO fundamentals AI won’t replace


Even as AI changes SEO, it won’t replace the fundamentals of maintaining technical accessibility, creating helpful, reliable, and people-first content, building brand authority, and applying human judgment to SEO initiatives.


### 1. Maintaining technical accessibility


Whether people look for answers with a search engine or an AI assistant, these systems generally discover content in the same way — which makes maintaining technical accessibility as important as ever.


Technical accessibility means improving your site infrastructure to help AI and search crawlers find, read, and understand your content. It involves three elements:


- **Crawlability** : Whether crawlers can reach your pages
- **Indexing** : Whether search platforms can add your content to their index — a database of information they draw on to answer queries
- **Accessible content** : Whether crawlers can read your content, including images


Some AI search platforms tap into search engine indexes to supplement their answers with live online data. For example, AI Overviews draw on Google’s search index, while[ChatGPT is known to use Google’s and Bing’s](https://www.semrush.com/blog/where-does-ai-get-its-information/) .


As a result, it’s important that search engines can access and index your content. If they can’t, the AI search platforms that rely on those indexes may not be able to retrieve it when they search the web.


#### How to maintain technical accessibility


To help AI and search crawlers read and understand your content, maintain technical accessibility by taking steps like these:


- **Review your**[robots.txt](https://www.semrush.com/blog/beginners-guide-robots-txt/) **file** : Check that this file doesn’t contain disallow rules telling AI and search crawlers not to crawl your site
- **Add descriptive image**[alternative (alt) text](https://www.semrush.com/blog/alt-text/) : This text helps crawlers better understand what your images show
- **Don’t use JavaScript to load essential content** : Many AI crawlers cannot execute JavaScript files


Then, check your website’s technical accessibility with a tool like Semrush’s[Site Audit](https://www.semrush.com/siteaudit/) , which scans for 140+ issues. In the “ **Issues** ” tab, you can filter the results by “ **AI Search** ,” “ **Crawlability** ,” or “ **Indexability** ” to narrow in on specific problems.


### 2. Creating helpful, reliable, and people-first content


Google has long encouraged SEOs to create “helpful, reliable, and people-first” content. It now uses a different label, called “non-commodity content,” in its guidance on[optimizing for AI search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide) , but the underlying quality principles largely remain the same.


Non-commodity content is content that provides unique insights based on personal expertise or experience, according to Google’s AI optimization guide. One example is Bon Appétit’s review of the best cutting boards, which doesn’t just list the winners, but also details the brand’s testing methodology and findings for each board.


In contrast, commodity content is content based on common knowledge, so generic that anyone could’ve written it. Like if someone publishes an article listing the best cutting boards without explaining how those boards made the cut.


Comparing Google’s criteria for creating non-commodity content in its AI optimization guide with its long-standing[guidance for creating helpful, reliable, and people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) shows significant overlap:


**Non-commodity content**


**Helpful, reliable, and people-first content**


Offers a unique point of view, not a summary of what’s already out there


Offers original information, research, or analysis


Goes beyond common knowledge


Goes beyond the obvious


Doesn’t recycle what others have said or what AI systems can easily produce


Adds substantial value instead of rewriting other sources


Shows experienced takes, like firsthand reviews


Shows firsthand expertise, like having used a product


This overlap in quality criteria is unsurprising, considering that Google bases its generative AI features, including AI Overviews, on its core Search ranking and quality systems.


The difference is that the stakes are now higher, because AI assistants and AI Overviews can provide complete answers to many queries — especially informational ones. Generic articles that repackage existing information give AI systems little reason to cite them. And people who encounter these articles may not bother clicking through.


#### How to create non-commodity content


To create non-commodity content worth citing and visiting, take steps like:


- **Publishing original data** from your own surveys, studies, or research
- **Including expert contributions** , like interview quotes, from subject matter experts within and outside of your organization
- **Testing products personally** , while sharing your methodology and findings
- **Documenting firsthand experiences** of tactics you’ve tried or situations you’ve navigated in the past, and what you learned
- **Adding bylines and author biographies** , and mentioning your sources, which helps readers trust your content


Focus on content quality, not quantity. Google’s AI optimization guide cautions that having many pages doesn’t always make a website higher quality.


### 3. Building brand authority


Brand authority is a well-established SEO consideration, and it also matters for AI search, since AI systems form their view of your brand from what’s published about it online.


Brand authority is a measure of how well known and reputable your brand is, based on factors like the number and quality of websites that mention your brand and link to your site. Search engines tend to rank authoritative sites higher because they view these websites as more trustworthy.


Meanwhile, AI search platforms ground their answers in content from across the wider internet, not just your site. In our study of 1,000 domains, we found a[strong positive correlation](https://www.semrush.com/blog/backlinks-ai-search-study/) between a site’s[Authority Score](https://www.semrush.com/kb/747-authority-score-backlink-scores) — our compound metric for a site’s backlink quality and related signals — and the number of AI mentions it got.


The correlation was especially strong among sites in the higher authority tiers.


Having more third-party sites, especially reputable ones, corroborate what you say about your brand also gives AI search platforms a clearer picture of it. They may then mention you in response to relevant prompts more often.


#### How to build brand authority


Build brand authority by strengthening your[brand visibility](https://www.semrush.com/blog/brand-visibility/) on third-party sites. Here’s how:


- **Claim directory listings** : Fill out your profiles on relevant platforms like Google Business Profile, Yelp, and Tripadvisor with accurate brand information, and keep them up to date
- **Run**[digital PR](https://www.semrush.com/blog/digital-pr/) **campaigns** : Pitch credible industry publications with original data or expert commentary to earn coverage
- **Take part in forums** : Contribute helpful insights to relevant discussions on community platforms like Reddit and Quora without overly promoting your brand


Keep your brand messaging consistent across all platforms you appear on, including your site and social media accounts. This way, they’ll corroborate the key facts and positioning you want AI systems to know and describe you by.


Then, check your site’s Authority Score with our[Domain Overview](https://www.semrush.com/analytics/overview/) tool. The higher the score, the more authoritative your site is. And the more visible it may be in AI search.


### 4. Applying human judgment to SEO initiatives


However capable AI becomes, we still need to apply human judgment to decide which SEO initiatives are worth pursuing before we direct AI accordingly.


In particular, these three areas call for human strategy:


- **What appeals to your audience** : Draw on your knowledge of your audience’s preferences and needs to choose the content angles and topics to cover
- **Where to invest** : The markets and platforms you target can have significant revenue impact, and AI assistants may not have a full view of your business operations
- **How to differentiate** : AI can analyze your strengths and your competitors’ weaknesses to identify gaps your brand can exploit. But whether your brand **should** exploit them involves a judgment call.


#### How to apply human judgment to SEO initiatives


Focus your own time on research, analysis, and strategy. For example:


- **Research your audience** : Review the questions users ask your sales and support teams, and interview select customers who fit your ideal customer profile
- **Analyze your visibility data** : Break down your search and AI visibility metrics by platform, country, and topic to see which gaps to close first
- **Pressure-test your positioning** : Compare how you and your competitors describe your offerings, and then ask customers which differences influence buying decisions


Once you’ve done this work, have your AI assistants automate the tasks that follow. You’ll save time that you can feed into subsequent rounds of research, analysis, and strategy, as the cycle repeats.


## Stay ahead as AI replaces SEO


AI can replace SEO. In fact, it’s already happening. But some fundamentals, including the basic need for search and discovery, are still relevant.


What matters is knowing which of these fundamentals to double down on and which parts of your business model to pivot. This way, you’ll apply the right strategies and invest in the right tools to stay visible as search evolves.

## FAQs


### Is SEO still worth it in 2027?


Yes, SEO is still worth it in 2027. Your brand needs to show up on the platforms your audience uses to search, whether that’s Google, YouTube, Reddit, TikTok, an AI assistant, or elsewhere. The SEO work you do to improve search visibility builds the foundation for that wider presence.


### Will SEO exist in five years?


Yes, SEO will still exist in five years. AI is changing where people search, not whether they search. Your audience’s preferred search platforms will keep evolving, so track where they turn for answers to the problems you solve and make sure your brand shows up there. This way, you’ll keep your sales pipeline healthy in the long run.


### Will AI replace SEO jobs?


AI may replace parts of SEO jobs, like keyword clustering, metadata generation, conducting basic technical audits, and reporting. But[SEOs are unlikely to be out of a job completely](https://www.semrush.com/blog/seo-job-market-study/) , as businesses still need people to exercise judgment on the SEO initiatives to pursue and to check AI’s output. If you’re an SEO, watch[where the industry is heading](https://www.semrush.com/blog/future-of-seo/) so you can build skills that help you stay relevant.


### Is SEO dead?


If “dead” means completely irrelevant, then no,[SEO isn’t dead](https://www.semrush.com/blog/is-seo-dead/) . SEO is still relevant as long as people continue to search. But AI is replacing parts of SEO, including some of the clicks that used to go to websites. Track how search platforms and behavior are changing, then adjust your strategy proactively.


### What’s the difference between SEO and GEO?


The difference between SEO and GEO is that SEO conventionally focuses on improving search engine rankings, while GEO generally refers to work that helps improve visibility across AI search platforms. In practice, both disciplines overlap substantially, with some marketers using “SEO” and “GEO” interchangeably. Either way, the underlying goal is the same: getting seen on the platforms where people search.


### Will ChatGPT replace Google?


ChatGPT is unlikely to fully replace Google. In[our study of Google usage after ChatGPT adoption](https://www.semrush.com/blog/google-usage-after-chatgpt-adoption/) , U.S. desktop users who started using ChatGPT in Q1 2025 didn’t search with Google less afterward. Their Google Search usage even rose by 2.1 sessions a week. People are adding ChatGPT to how they search instead of replacing Google with it.
